survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive results and proficiency-level shares for Türkiye based on the PISA 2022 assessment design. The note describes that PISA uses complex sampling across participating countries/economies and that estimates are accompanied by uncertainty (e.g., 95% confidence intervals), implying the use of PISA’s sampling/estimation procedures. However, the factsheet does not specify the exact student weight variable name(s) or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used. For analysts working with PISA microdata, the recommended approach is to apply the official PISA student sampling weights and replicate weights provided in the PISA database when producing standard errors and confidence intervals; this factsheet itself does not document those technical details.

As such, it does not provide a methodological description of plausible-value (PV) handling or missing-data procedures for an ML pipeline. The absence of PV/missing-data documentation here is therefore a reporting scope limitation specific to a results factsheet, not evidence that such procedures were not used in the underlying PISA production process.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet for Türkiye summarizes how 15-year-old students performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed over time (notably 2018 to 2022 and comparisons to earlier cycles such as 2012, 2006, and 2015). Students took two two-hour tests with different subject combinations across students, and they also completed a background questionnaire; school principals completed a separate questionnaire. The factsheet reports mean performance trends, proficiency-level attainment (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and within-country gaps by socio-economic status and gender, with uncertainty communicated via confidence intervals. It also flags that PISA 2022 was delayed to 2022 due to COVID-19 and that some countries/economies may have sampling-standard issues (Türkiye is stated to have met quality standards). No student-level machine learning models are estimated in this factsheet; it is intended for policy interpretation of descriptive benchmarks rather than causal or predictive inference.
